name.value: Vanderhoof Tourism and Cultural Centre & Community Museum

description.value: The Vanderhoof Tourism and Cultural Centre is situated on the museum grounds along Highway 16, making it a natural stop for cycle-tourers on the Yellowhead corridor. The site features a striking 12-metre wooden carving by master carver Peter Rodseth alongside historical exhibits from the Nechako Valley and Saik'uz First Nation. Visitor centre staff offer regional maps and travel information, and a 1.25 km Heritage Nature Trail loops through the museum grounds along Stoney Creek.

The OSM name 'Vanderhoof Museum' differs from the website's full name 'Vanderhoof Tourism and Cultural Centre & Community Museum'. No bike parking, washrooms, or water amenities are explicitly described anywhere in the fetched content; the only parking reference is 'large trailer parking available behind the site,' which does not confirm bike-specific infrastructure.
